title: hybrid-map-compactifier-and-spill-attenuation
author: Evelyn Chen
description:
Motivation: Long-running tenants and variable sequence workloads expose pathological KV cache fragmentation and recurring micro-spill events that increase tail latency and IO spikes during eviction. This PR introduces a hybrid map compactifier plus an attenuation layer for spill-over that cooperates with continuous-batching to smooth reclaim pressure and preserve P99 latency.

What this changes (single-line list): 
- Adds a HybridMapCompactifier that performs low-cost in-place compaction for small segments and async remap compaction for large sparse ranges.
- Introduces a SpillAttenuationController: token-bucket backpressure on spill operations with hysteresis and per-tenant fairness weights.
- Evictor policy: age+density scoring and a secondary soft-throttle to prefer coalescing evictions into larger contiguous ranges to reduce write amplification.
- Scheduler hint: a kernel_prefer_local flag exposes low-latency kernel selection for compaction work to reduce kernel-launch jitter on multi-GPU hosts.
- Continuous batching integration: compaction and spill tasks are batched with inference prefix batching windows to avoid competing for GPU kernel time during high QPS.
- Tests & benchmarks: microbenchmarks for fragmentation scenarios and an e2e bench that simulates tenant churn.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation and unit tests for compactifier and controller
- [x] Integration with evictor scoring and scheduler hints
- [x] Benchmark harness and regression guardrail (quality + perf)
- [x] Documentation (runtime/kv_allocator/README updated)
- [x] Add Linear references and attach workload traces used for tuning

Performance summary (compared to main, workload: mixed-seq churn RPS 5k): 
- Median memory residency reduced by ~7% due to in-place compaction and coalesced evictions.
- P99 tail latency for inference generation while background compaction is active improved from 132ms to 92ms (=~30% reduction).
- Spill IO peaks reduced by ~55% because SpillAttenuationController batches and rate-limits spill windows.
- CPU overhead for allocator background threads + compaction is ~3% of host CPU on our bench machines.

Why this is different: Existing strategies either run aggressive global compaction (high cost) or rely solely on eviction heuristics. The hybrid compactifier keeps hot small objects contiguous cheaply while async remapping handles large sparse regions; combined with attenuation it minimizes IO storms during reclaim.

Notes on deployments and safety: 
- Feature gated behind runtime flag kv.enable_hybrid_compactifier=false by default for canary rollout.
- SpillAttenuationController exposes two tunables (burst_tokens, refill_ms) with safe defaults used in Dedicated clusters.
- No breaking API changes; config additions are additive.

Related work / tickets: Linear ENG-1981 (fragmentation regression), ENG-2027 (spillback rate-limiter), ENG-2064 (batching integration), SUP-87 referenced for a customer incident that motivated the attenuation design.
